label: Haiku 5.5, shipped prompt, one request at a time
note: Latency run: dev passages, sequential, fresh calls (run with --fresh --concurrency 1).

items.text: 黛玉冷笑道：「我就知道，別人不挑剩下的也不給我。」
items.answer: Dai-yu sneered, "I knew it. Unless the others have picked over everything first, I'm not given anything."

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Phoenix said, "I've been telling you all day long that you're too soft. Letting the household people get this out of hand, how can it be allowed?"

errors.evidence: Phoenix said
errors.why: 鳳姐 is rendered as 'Phoenix', an unexplained translation of the nickname; the reader expects Xifeng.

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long
errors.why: 成日家 means 'constantly', and 'all day long' with the present perfect is slightly awkward, though the meaning is close.

errors.evidence: the household people
errors.why: 家裡人 here means household servants, and 'household people' is vague and could read as family members.

items.text: 寶玉未及回言，只見舡頭上來了兩人，一僧一道，夾住寶玉說道：「俗緣已畢，還不快走。」
items.answer: Before Baoyu could answer, two men came up to the prow of the boat, one a monk and one a Daoist. They pinned Baoyu between them and said, "Your worldly ties are over. Why not leave at once?"

items.text: 平兒笑道：「『得饒人處且饒人』，得省的將就些事也罷了。
items.answer: Ping'er laughed and said, "'Where you can let people off, let them off.' It would be just as well to overlook a few things and let them go."

items.text: 黛玉道：「不曾讀，只上了一年學，些須認得幾個字。」
items.answer: "I haven't studied," Daiyu said. "I only attended school for a year, and I can recognize a few characters."

items.text: 因此劉姥姥看不過，乃勸道：「姑爺，你別嗔著我多嘴。
items.answer: So Granny Liu could not hold her tongue, and she spoke up: "Son-in-law, don't be cross with me for running my mouth.

errors.evidence: could not hold her tongue
errors.why: 看不過 means she could not bear to watch or stand it, not that she could not keep quiet; the nuance of 勸 (advise) is also reduced to 'spoke up'.

items.text: 李貴笑道：“不怕你老人家惱我，素日你老人家到底有些不正經，所以這些兄弟才不聽。
items.answer: Li Gui laughed and said, "Don't blame me for speaking plainly, young master, but you have never been entirely proper in your ways, and that is why these young fellows won't listen to you."

errors.evidence: young master
errors.why: The source says 你老人家, a respectful address, not 'young master'; the term is invented and does not fit Jia Rui's status as a senior student.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: having gone through a dream-like experience, I have hidden the true events and borrowed the tale of the spirit-stone to write this book, The Story of the Stone.

errors.evidence: having gone through a dream-like experience, I have hidden the true events
errors.why: Pronoun shifts from third person ('The author says') to first person 'I', and the participial clause dangles; the reference keeps third person.

errors.evidence: a dream-like experience
errors.why: Loses the sense of 'once' (曾) and the sequence 'after' (之後), so the experience preceding the writing is only weakly conveyed.

items.text: 孫悟空在傍聞講，喜得他抓耳撓腮，眉花眼笑，忍不住手之舞之，足之蹈之。
items.answer: Sun Wukong, listening from the side, was so delighted that he tweaked his ears and scratched his cheeks, his brows dancing and his eyes beaming, and he could not help but wave his hands and stamp his feet.

items.text: 有一般天罡數，該三十六般變化；有一般地煞數，該七十二般變化。
items.answer: There is a set of Heavenly Gang numbers, which governs thirty-six transformations; there is a set of Earthly Sha numbers, which governs seventy-two transformations.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。
items.answer: Wukong said, "Ever since I learned the Way, I have acquired the power of seventy-two earthly transformations, and my somersault cloud has boundless magical power. I am skilled at concealing my body and escaping from sight, and at summoning and subduing by spell.

items.text: 卻說他師徒兩個策馬前來，直至山門首觀看，果然是一座寺院。
items.answer: Now the two of them, master and disciple, rode their horses up to the gate and looked closely. It was indeed a temple.

items.text: 卻說那個妖王在洞裡歡喜道：「小的們，孫行者吃了虧去了。
items.answer: Now the demon king inside the cave said happily, "You lot, Sun the Monkey has taken a beating and gone off."

errors.evidence: Sun the Monkey
errors.why: 孫行者 is Sun the Pilgrim; "the Monkey" swaps his title for a nickname, though the character is still identifiable.

errors.evidence: has taken a beating
errors.why: 吃了虧 means he came off worst or suffered a setback, not necessarily that he was physically beaten, so the rendering is slightly too specific.

items.text: 卻說三藏自貞觀十三年九月望前三日，蒙唐王與多官送出長安關外。
items.answer: Now, to speak of Tripitaka: on the third day before the full moon of the ninth month of the thirteenth year of the Zhenguan era, the Tang King and many officials escorted him out beyond the pass at Chang'an.

items.text: 孔明囑付曰：「吾受劉皇叔三顧之恩，不容不出。
items.answer: Kongming charged him, saying: "I have received Liu Huangshu's kindness in calling on me three times, and I cannot but come out to serve."

errors.evidence: Liu Huangshu's kindness
errors.why: The title 劉皇叔 is left as pinyin "Huangshu", which reads like a personal name and hides its meaning of "Imperial Uncle".

items.text: 玄德曰：「備乃中山靖王之後；自涿郡剿戮黃巾，大小三十餘戰，頗有微功，因得除今職。」
items.answer: "Xuande said, 'I am a descendant of the Prince of Zhongshan, Jing. Since I slaughtered the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo Commandery, I have fought more than thirty battles, big and small, and earned some modest merit, which is how I was appointed to my present post.'"

errors.evidence: the Prince of Zhongshan, Jing
errors.why: The title is awkwardly ordered; the standard form is "Prince Jing of Zhongshan", and the definite article suggests a single known person.

errors.evidence: Since I slaughtered the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo Commandery
errors.why: 自涿郡 means starting from Zhuo Commandery, not that the slaughter happened there, and 剿戮 means to suppress or exterminate. The rendering is slightly off but the overall meaning is kept.

items.text: 玄德曰：「我與民秋毫無犯，那得財物與他？」
items.answer: "I have not taken so much as a hair's worth from the people," Xuande said. "Where would I get money to give him?"

items.text: 馬謖在山上見之，大笑曰：「彼若有命，不來圍山。」
items.answer: Ma Su, watching from the mountain, laughed and said, "If he had any sense, he would not come to surround the mountain."

errors.evidence: If he had any sense, he would not come to surround the mountain.
errors.why: 有命 means 'if he values his life / has fate to live', not 'has sense', though the mocking implication is similar.

errors.evidence: laughed and said
errors.why: 大笑 'laughed loudly' is reduced to 'laughed', and 'saw him' is only implied by 'watching'.

items.text: 張飛性起，向玄德換了坐下馬，搶出陣來，叫曰：「我捉你不得，誓不上關！」
items.answer: Zhang Fei, roused to fury, swapped his mount with Xuande's, rushed out before the lines, and shouted, "I cannot capture you, so I swear I will not return to the pass!"

errors.evidence: I cannot capture you, so I swear I will not return to the pass!
errors.why: The conditional oath ('if I can't capture you, I won't go up') becomes a causal statement of fact, so the sense of 'not until I succeed' is lost.

items.text: 行到赤岸坡，見蜀兵已去遠，乃引還，顧謂眾將曰：「孔明已死，我等皆高枕無憂矣！」
items.answer: When they reached Chi'an Slope and saw the Shu troops had already gone far away, he turned his army back. Looking at his generals, he said, "Zhuge Liang is dead, and now we can all sleep easy with no worries!"

items.text: 武松道：「只好恁地，卻又來望哥哥。」
items.answer: "That's all I can do for now. I'll come back to see my brother."

errors.evidence: That's all I can do for now.
errors.why: 只好恁地 means 'this much will do/enough', not an inability; the nuance of declining more drink is shifted.

items.text: 智深尋思道：「這個大寺，如何敗落的恁地？」
items.answer: Zhishen thought to himself, "How could such a great temple have fallen into such ruin?"

items.text: 魯達道：「恁地時，洒家自去便了。」
items.answer: "Then I'll just go on my own," said Lu Da.

items.text: 宋江道：「兄弟，卻是你殺了小衙內，雖是軍師嚴令，論齒序他也是你哥哥，且看我面，與他伏個禮，我卻自拜你便了。」
items.answer: "Brother, it was you who killed the little young master. Though it was the military counselor's strict order, by age he is still your elder brother. Do it for my sake and give him a bow. Then I will bow to you myself, and that will do."

errors.evidence: the little young master
errors.why: Redundant, awkward rendering of 小衙內; "young master" alone would be natural.

items.text: 酒家道：「客官，你須見我門前招旗上面明明寫道：『三碗不過岡』。」
items.answer: The innkeeper said, "Sir, you must have seen the banner in front of my door, where it clearly says: 'Three bowls and you cannot pass the ridge.'"

items.text: 戴宗連忙回轉身來問道：「壯士素不曾拜識，如何呼喚賤名？」
items.answer: Dai Zong quickly turned around and asked, "Brave sir, we have never met, so how do you know my humble name?"

items.text: 見我管待客人在此喫酒，你便與他三五升米便了，何須直來問我！」
items.answer: "Can't you see I'm entertaining guests here over drinks? You should just give him three or five sheng of rice and be done with it. Why come straight to me to ask?"

items.text: 鲁镇的酒店的格局，是和别处不同的：都是当街一个曲尺形的大柜台，柜里面豫备着热水，可以随时温酒。
items.answer: The wine shops in Luzhen were laid out differently from those elsewhere: each had a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square facing the street, with hot water kept ready inside the counter so that wine could be warmed at any time.

items.text: 到了年关，掌柜取下粉板说：『孔乙己还欠十九个钱呢！』
items.answer: When the year-end came, the shopkeeper took down the blackboard and said, "Kong Yiji still owes nineteen coins!"

items.text: 孔乙己便涨红了脸，额上的青筋条条绽出，争辩道：『窃书不能算偸……窃书！……读书人的事，能算偸么？』
items.answer: Kong Yiji flushed red in the face, the veins on his forehead standing out one by one, and protested: "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... stealing books! ...Is it stealing when it comes to a scholar's affairs?"

errors.evidence: "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... stealing books!"
errors.why: Both 窃书 and 偸 are rendered as "stealing", so the contrast between the refined word and the plain one is lost and Kong Yiji's argument becomes self-contradictory.

errors.evidence: the veins on his forehead standing out one by one
errors.why: The "blue" (青) of the veins is not conveyed.

items.text: 又好笑，又不耐烦，懒懒的答他道：『谁要你教，不是草头底下一个来回的回字么？』
items.answer: "Half amused and half impatient, I answered him lazily, 'Who asked you to teach me? Isn't it the 回 in 来回, the one under the grass radical?'"

items.text: 我的父亲允许了；我也很高兴，因为我早听到闰土这名字，而且知道他和我仿佛年纪，闰月生的，五行缺土，所以他的父亲叫他闰土。
items.answer: My father agreed, and I was glad too, because I had long heard the name Runtu, and I knew he was about my age. He was born in an intercalary month, and since his five elements lacked earth, his father named him Runtu.

items.text: 现在我所谓希望，不也是我自己手制的偶像么？
items.answer: Now what I call hope, is it not an idol I made with my own hands?

items.text: 我看出他话中全是毒，笑中全是刀，他们的牙齿，全是白厉厉的排着，这就是吃人的家伙。
items.answer: I saw that his words were all poison and his smiles all knives. Their teeth were all lined up, gleaming white and menacing, and these were the fangs of man-eaters.

errors.evidence: these were the fangs of man-eaters
errors.why: 家伙 means 'creature/tool' (man-eating things); 'fangs' narrows it and the teeth are made the man-eaters' possession, losing the dehumanizing/instrument sense.

items.text: 我也不怕；虽然不吃人，胆子却比他们还壮。
items.answer: I am not afraid either. Though I do not eat people, my courage is greater than theirs.

items.text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
items.answer: The Master said, "To learn and at due times practice what you have learned, is this not a pleasure? To have friends come from afar, is this not a joy? To be unknown by others and yet not be resentful, is this not the mark of a gentleman?"

items.text: 子曰：「巧言令色，鮮矣仁。」
items.answer: The Master said, "Those who are glib in speech and ingratiating in manner are seldom truly benevolent."

items.text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而愼於言，就有道而正焉：可謂好學也已。」
items.answer: The Master said, "A gentleman does not seek a full belly in his food, nor comfort in his dwelling. He is quick in his work and careful in his speech, and he seeks out those who have the Way and sets himself right by them. Such a man may indeed be called fond of learning."

items.text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也。未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也」。
items.answer: Zigong said, "What about someone who is poor but does not flatter, and rich but is not arrogant?" The Master said, "That is acceptable. But it is not as good as someone who is poor yet delights in the Way, or rich yet loves ritual."

items.text:
牀前明月光，疑是地上霜。
舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉。
items.answer:
Before my bed, the bright moonlight,
I wonder if it is frost on the ground.
I raise my head and gaze at the bright moon;
I lower my head and think of my homeland.

items.text:
紅豆生南國，春來發幾枝。
願君多采擷，此物最相思。
items.answer:
Red beans grow in the southern land;
When spring comes, how many branches they send forth.
I beg you, pick them often,
For of all things, this one stirs longing most.

errors.evidence: I beg you, pick them often,
errors.why: 多采擷 means gather plenty of them, not pick them often (frequency), though the wish to gather is kept.

errors.evidence: how many branches they send forth.
errors.why: The question is rendered as a statement-like clause with a period, so the wondering tone of 幾枝 is weakened.

items.text:
千山鳥飛絕，萬徑人蹤滅。
孤舟簑笠翁，獨釣寒江雪。
items.answer:
A thousand mountains, no birds flying.
Ten thousand paths, no trace of a person.
A lone boat, an old man in a straw cape and hat,
Fishing alone in the cold river snow.
